Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players have made their way out in the middle followed by the Afghan batters - Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Hazratullah Zazai. Aayan Khan comes to bowl. Lets go...
...THE CHASE...

Right then! UAE are aware of how the pitch is playing. If they take 2-3 wickets early on and execute their plans well, they could make a match out of this one. An entertaining second half coming up. Stay tuned.

Qais Ahmad is in for a chat. He says that he went according to the plan to get Waseem. Adds that he kept the length right and handled the pressure well. He says that they will look to chase the score and the wicket is turning a bit. Ends by saying that the glasses he is wearing are specifically for the night games.

Afghanistan would have taken this score at the start. They will be confident to win this game but, certainly, the victory won't come easy as the pitch has a lot of demons in it. It is swinging, turning and stays low a lot as well. Afghanistan bowled well, could have kept United Arab Emirates below 100 but still have done well.

A competitive total by UAE. Mind you this is not an easy pitch to bat on and UAE will be happy with the total. Would have loved more as they chose to bat first on a pitch which was a treat for the bowlers. UAE lost wickets regularly and were five down at the halfway stage. At one point, even 100 looked difficult but the tail stood up for UAE. The bottom six contributed most of the runs and made sure they end with a decent total.
Shorter and on middle, Jawadullah pulls it to deep square leg for a couple of run. United Arab Emirates end with 126 for 9.

So, we are into the decider of the Afghanistan tour of the United Arab Emirates. The United Arab Emirates team will be aiming for a strong performance in this match to secure the series win. They will rely on captain Muhammad Waseem and stand-in opener Aryan Lakra to provide a solid start. In the last game, despite a slow start in scoring boundaries, they managed to accumulate runs steadily. The United Arab Emirates bowlers initially struggled, but later managed to take wickets at regular intervals, ultimately securing a win. The team will be hoping for another strong all-round performance to achieve their elusive series victory. The Afghan bowlers initially struggled to pick wickets in the powerplay but took crucial wickets to prevent the middle order from capitalizing. Despite restricting the United Arab Emirates to 166/7, Afghanistan's openers, particularly Hazratullah Zazai, started strong in the chase. However, they struggled against Ali Naseer who ran havoc over their top order. They lost 6 wickets with only 52 runs added. With 6 overs left and 4 wickets in hand, Afghanistan needed 70 runs, relying on Mohammad Nabi. Despite Nabi's efforts, Afghanistan ultimately fell short in their chase by just 11 runs. Afghanistan dominated all aspects of the game in the series opener, securing a 72-run victory. However, United Arab Emirates showed resilience and made a strong comeback to win the second match. With the series tied at 1-1, the competition is finely balanced, and the decider promises to be a cracking one.
